notes:
Summary: evaluation for Dedicated capacity to support cross-jurisdiction legal search + assistant. Primary ask: predictable unit economics for embeddings-heavy workload and 95th PCT latency SLOs for short chat queries.

Background/Biz driver:
- Penumbra builds a legal research assistant used by large law firms and corporate legal teams. Customer data includes contracts and filings (PII + confidential).
- Need private deployment options for EU and some on-prem for top-tier clients. Compliance is a gating item.

Technical requirements (from product call 2026-02-11):
- Workloads: embeddings for semantic search (batch of ~10k docs / day), reranking on top-k results, chat assistant concurrent sessions ~400-600, spikes to 1.2k qps during peak research hours.
- Latency targets: chat P95 <= 200ms for short prompts (<128 tokens) for enterprise tier; embeddings indexing jobs are throughput-oriented (>= 200 docs/sec when indexing).
- Throughput guarantees: want committed baseline 500 qps sustained; ability to burst to 1.2k qps within 2 minutes.
- Hardware: asking for estimate of number of 80GB GPUs (A100/H800 class) and guidance on mixed GPU pools vs homogeneous. Prefer reserved pool with warm KV cache nodes.

Cost modeling discussion notes (SE session 2026-02-25):
- We walked through Redwood's commit tiers: 4x, 8x, 16x GPU equivalents mapped to qps estimates.
- Penumbra's baseline traffic map -> modeled need of ~8x 80GB GPUs for steady-state (embeddings + chat) assuming 60% average utilization; spikes require temporary burst capacity or fallback to hosted cheaper variant.
- Unit economics: SE showed sample per-token cost: $0.0005/token for rtx-quantized variant at 60% util vs $0.0012/token at 25% util. Team requested a per-conversation cost model (tokens per convo ~450 avg).
- Break-even horizon: with a 12-month commit at estimated ARR $350k, committed GPUs reduce unit cost ~35% vs on-demand.

SLA & negotiation points (notes from AE/legal sync 2026-03-04):
- Penumbra pushing for 99.9% availability for dedicated pool and P95 latency credits: 10% credit per 10 basis-point miss (capped at 50%). Redwood standard is 99.5% for dedicated; AE proposed 99.85% for platinum tier + 45-day cure window.
- Measurability: need shared dashboard (token-level traces) and audit logs exported to customer SIEM. SE: can supply per-route dashboards + routing logs; legal wants explicit log retention period (12 months) and export SLA.

POC plan & timeline:
- POC 8-week plan agreed in principle: weeks 0-2: deploy private control plane in Penumbra VPC (staging), weeks 3-5: ingest 100k doc corpus + run indexing at controlled cadence, weeks 6-8: simulate traffic for 500 qps and run failover/fallback tests.
- Success criteria: sustained 500 qps for 24h with P95 latency <220ms, <2% error rate, and no KV cache invalidation on reboots.

Numbers / example model used in cost sheet (hand-off from SE):
- Baseline: 8 x 80GB GPUs reserved, price = $18,000/GPU-month (example), commit discount 30% for 12-mo -> effective $12,600/GPU-month -> monthly committed cost = $100,800.
- Assumptions: average utilization 60%, total tokens/month ~180M, tokens per second aligned to qps and prompt sizes.
- Derived unit price = committed_monthly_cost / tokens_per_month -> $100,800 / 180,000,000 = $0.00056/token.
- Sensitivity: if utilization falls to 40% unit price -> $0.00084/token; if utilization rises to 80% -> $0.00042/token.

Path to close & open items:
- Pricing: need 3yr topline option; finance to provide TCO vs cloud-hosted infra. (blocked: finance modeling inputs from Penumbra).
- Legal: finish data residency and liability language for EU client on-prem deployments. (blocked: Penumbra legal to provide requested amendments).
- Tech: confirm warm KV cache architecture and cold-start behavior for model variants; provide runbook for cache pre-warm. (SE action item).
